title: Why Multilatinas Are Becoming More American
gist: A lawyer argues Latin American multilatinas are responding to US tariff policy by becoming more American, through US industrial investment, financial integration (Nu Holdings) and structural realignment (Cementos Argos split). Examples include Bimbo, Techint, Gerdau and Cencosud.

insights.claim: Instead of lobbying, retaliating or retreating in response to US tariffs, multilatinas are choosing integration, becoming legally and operationally more American through industrial deepening, financial integration and structural realignment.
insights.speaker: CONRADO TENAGLIA
insights.so_what: Read-through: LatAm corporates view US assets as the stable growth market; expect more US-based capex and listings.
insights.quote: becoming, in a legal and operational sense, more American

insights.claim: Grupo Bimbo plans about $1 billion of US investment in 2026-2028; Bimbo Bakeries USA already runs over 50 plants with over 20,000 employees.
insights.speaker: CONRADO TENAGLIA
insights.so_what: Concrete US capex commitment from a Mexican staples company.

insights.claim: Techint's Tenaris reactivated heat-treatment and finishing lines at its Pennsylvania mill in January for US energy pipes, Ternium is expanding in Pesqueria, Mexico for US auto and construction demand, and Gerdau is spending $51.5 million in Texas for data-center and renewables build-out.
insights.speaker: CONRADO TENAGLIA
insights.so_what: Steel producers are localizing in the US ahead of tariff barriers, tied to energy and data-center demand.

insights.claim: Nu Holdings opened for business in the US through a partnership with Lead Bank, and its own US national bank charter was conditionally approved by the OCC in January.
insights.speaker: CONRADO TENAGLIA
insights.so_what: Nubank's US entry is a catalyst for the Latin American fintech story.
insights.locator: Nu Holdings, Latin America's largest digital bank

insights.claim: Cementos Argos announced in April it would split into Argos Latam and US-based Argos Materials, a template others may follow once their US business reaches scale for independent capital structures and regulators.
insights.speaker: CONRADO TENAGLIA
insights.so_what: Watch for similar spin-offs, which can unlock valuation of US assets.

insights.claim: Alsea, which runs Starbucks in Latin America and Europe under licensing agreements extended to 2046, represents a different model: a long-term partnership with a US brand as growth engine.
insights.speaker: CONRADO TENAGLIA
insights.so_what: Long-dated license extension de-risks the franchise model.

insights.claim: US tariff policy has had uneven effects: Mexico faces anxiety over USMCA, now on an annual review basis; Brazil has borne significant costs; Argentina, Uruguay, Ecuador and several Central American economies have gained by aligning with US standards.
insights.speaker: CONRADO TENAGLIA
insights.so_what: Winners and losers differ by alignment with Washington.
insights.locator: The U.S. remains, by a wide margin

insights.claim: The first multilatina, Bunge y Born, emerged a century ago in Argentina when it controlled a fifth of world wheat trade; internationalization revived in the 1990s with Chilean firms such as Falabella.
insights.speaker: CONRADO TENAGLIA
insights.so_what: Historical context for the corporate wave.

insights.claim: Cencosud bought 67% of US premium grocer The Fresh Market in 2022 for $676 million, retaining local management, showing the evolution from exporting formats to buying a platform in the US.
insights.speaker: CONRADO TENAGLIA
insights.so_what: Precedent for control acquisitions of US platforms by LatAm retailers.

insights.claim: Domestic instability forged discipline in multilatinas that now helps them thrive in and alongside the US, so their pragmatism may prove their greatest strength as the global order grows unpredictable.
insights.speaker: CONRADO TENAGLIA
insights.quote: institutional fragility need not be a death sentence

insights.claim: An IDB study found multilatinas operate in 116 countries across sectors from food and energy to banking and aerospace.
insights.speaker: CONRADO TENAGLIA
insights.locator: A recent study by the Inter-American Development Bank
